fatal_errors: The proposed dual-phase FCC/BCC lamellar HEA is not the target Pd nanocube supported, approximately equiatomic PtRuFeCoNi high-entropy-alloy shell.
Surface functionalization is asserted instead of epitaxial deposition of a roughly 1 nm, randomly mixed FCC shell on {100}-faceted Pd nanocubes.
The mechanism omits near-thermoneutral hydrogen adsorption, orbital hybridization, the multielement cocktail effect, Ru-centered HER activity, and Pt/Co/Ni involvement in HOR.
No electrolyte, potential, temperature, composition, or cycling conditions are specified.
All cited evidence concerns structural, corrosion, or mechanical properties of unrelated HEAs and provides no evidence for HER or HOR performance.
The hypothesis gives no specific comparator or quantitative activity and durability prediction.
explanation: The response recognizes only the broad topic that an HEA might enhance HER and HOR activity and durability. It does not identify Pd@PtRuFeCoNi nanocubes or reconstruct their thin {100}-terminated metastable FCC shell, synthesis, operating conditions, active-site chemistry, thermal-ordering boundary, or quantitative superiority over Pt/C and other quinary shells. Its FCC/BCC lamellar microstructure is taken from an unrelated bulk AlCoCrFeNi structural alloy. The proposed experiment is merely a generic performance test and lacks matched controls, ECSA normalization, operando spectroscopy, adsorption-energy tests, and explicit thresholds. Because the cited papers do not address HER/HOR catalysis, the central catalytic claim is unsupported.
